A_target.statement:
Let $\phi_0 \paren \alpha = \omega^\alpha$ and let $\phi_{\beta + 1}$ enumerate the [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed points]] of $\phi_\beta$.
Then each $\phi_\beta$ is a [[Definition:Normal Function|normal function]], giving the [[Definition:Veblen Hierarchy|Veblen hierarchy]].

B_source.statement:
Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Normal Function|normal function]] on the [[Definition:Ordinal|ordinals]].
Then for every $\alpha$:
:$\displaystyle \sup_{n \mathop < \omega} \map {f^n} \alpha$
is a fixed point of $f$, and $f$ has arbitrarily large fixed points.

substitutions.the normal function: the enumerating function at the current level of the hierarchy
substitutions.the fixed points obtained by iteration: the ordinals enumerated at the next level
substitutions.the starting point of the iteration: an arbitrary ordinal, giving fixed points above it

derived.the class of fixed points: a closed unbounded class, itself enumerated by a normal function
derived.iterating the construction: the levels of the Veblen hierarchy

object_map.reformulation: Define each level as the enumeration of the points left unmoved by the previous level.

validity_conditions: A normal function is increasing and continuous at limits, so iterating it from any ordinal and taking the supremum lands on a fixed point.
The fixed point class is closed and unbounded, so it is itself enumerated by a normal function, which is what allows the construction to be iterated transfinitely.
Continuity at limits is essential: without it the supremum of the iterates need not be fixed, and the hierarchy would not be well defined.
proof_plan: $\phi_0 \paren \alpha = \omega^\alpha$ is [[Definition:Strictly Increasing Mapping|strictly increasing]] and continuous at limits, so is [[Definition:Normal Function|normal]].
By the [[Fixed Point Lemma for Normal Functions]], iterating $\phi_\beta$ from any $\alpha$ and taking the supremum gives a fixed point above $\alpha$.

The class of fixed points of a normal function is [[Definition:Closed Unbounded Class|closed and unbounded]].
Hence its enumerating function $\phi_{\beta + 1}$ is normal.
